entries.finding: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): P 16.0343 d; Christiansen et al. 2022 (2022AJ....163..244C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CHRISTIANSEN_ET_AL_2022): a/R* 39.39; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 88.79817 degrees; No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular; Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2457304.2922 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 235 min); Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north)..
